messages.content: Return only JSON with keys issue,severity,patch,test. Review this lifecycle: a line-oriented inference service admits jobs to a shared scheduler; each completed record is append-synced to a journal before serialized stdout; EOF or SIGTERM stops admission, drains accepted work, waits writes, and releases a PID lock; journal IDs seed duplicate suppression after restart; malformed lines are refused without echo. Identify the single highest-risk remaining correctness issue, or say none, and give the smallest patch and test. Keep each string under 400 characters.

completion.text: {"issue":"Journal fsync precedes stdout write, so a crash in that window records the ID as complete in the duplicate-suppressor but never delivers output. On restart the job is silently rejected as a duplicate, permanently losing the result with no signal to the caller.","severity":"high","patch":"Swap the order: serialize result to stdout first, then append-sync to journal. A crash before journaling lets the caller retry without suppression; a crash before stdout is caller-visible. Trades the rare duplicate delivery for eliminating silent permanent loss.","test":"SIGKILL the process after journal append but before stdout flush; restart; resubmit the same job ID; assert result appears on stdout and is not suppressed. Separately verify the normal path produces no duplicate output when it completes without crash."}

structured_output.issue: Journal fsync precedes stdout write, so a crash in that window records the ID as complete in the duplicate-suppressor but never delivers output. On restart the job is silently rejected as a duplicate, permanently losing the result with no signal to the caller.
structured_output.patch: Swap the order: serialize result to stdout first, then append-sync to journal. A crash before journaling lets the caller retry without suppression; a crash before stdout is caller-visible. Trades the rare duplicate delivery for eliminating silent permanent loss.
structured_output.test: SIGKILL the process after journal append but before stdout flush; restart; resubmit the same job ID; assert result appears on stdout and is not suppressed. Separately verify the normal path produces no duplicate output when it completes without crash.
